title: Football, Memory, and Mental Health: Players, Brain Imaging, and CTE
booktitle: Special Topic: Cognitive and Clinical Neuroscience
takeaways: Attention, episodic memory, executive control, mood, behavior, and independence require distinct observations and a timeline of change.
Reported difficulty, direct testing, and family observations describe complementary aspects of functioning; sensory and motor prerequisites can change task responses.
Structural MRI measures anatomy, diffusion MRI estimates water-motion properties, fMRI measures blood-oxygenation changes, and PET records tracer distribution.
Average differences between former players and controls do not establish an accurate individual CTE test. Clinical syndrome criteria and confirmed tissue pathology are different standards.
Alzheimer disease, Parkinson disease, depression, sleep disturbance, pain, and medication effects can contribute to symptoms in a former player.
Care can address symptoms and daily functioning while pathology remains uncertain. CTE-specific diagnostic and treatment claims require independent validation and appropriate clinical evidence.
